articles.title: Four no more: macOS 27.3 kills off those stupidly insecure certificates
articles.description: In the wake of the shockingly insecure security certificate fiasco, Apple has now completely blocked the compromised eMudhra certificates in macOS 27.3. The security certificates were far from secure. In October, security researchers discovered that a number of certificates issued by one certificate authority were woefully insecure, to an obscene degree. While Apple has worked to block the certificates from being used, the current developer beta round goes one stage further. After the discovery of the astoundingly weak certificates, Apple was able to stop the affected certificates from being used on iOS, iPadOS, and its other operating systems. However, as the curl utility in macOS doesn't check revocation information, Macs that had previously trusted the certificates would continue to do so, despite Apple's measures. Continue Reading on AppleInsider | Discuss on our Forums

articles.title: IEC puts backup power measures in place ahead of vote counting
articles.description: IEC puts backup power measures in place ahead of vote counting Zandile. Khumalo Wed, 11/04/2026 - 19:25 MIDRAND - The Electoral Commission of South Africa (IEC) has assured that contingency measures are in place to ensure that voting and the subsequent counting process are not disrupted by electricity outages. Briefing the media on Wednesday, just a few hours before voting stations close at 9pm, IEC Chief Electoral Officer Sy Mamabolo said generators and alternative lighting facilities have been made available to voting stations in areas that have experienced power outages. READ | Elections 2026 | Voices from the ground Mamabolo has praised the turnout of voters for the 2026 local government elections, with its preliminary estimates recording approximately 12 million voters who have cast their votes across the country as of 5pm today. But even so, with voting scheduled to close at 9pm, Mamabolo has urged eligible voters who have not yet cast their ballots to make their way to their registered voting stations. “The Commission reassures voters that anyone who arrives at a voting station before nine will be allowed to vote, even if the voting process extends beyond the official time of nine o'clock. This means every voter who is in the queue by the time of closing will not be turned away,” he said.
